subject: ACME: Audit log export format & evidence delivery — next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Anna Jones <anna.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Recap — audit log requirements & immediate next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Anna — great to meet you and Tim. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on scope for the audit-log deliverable we discussed.

Summary of what ACME asked for (from my notes):
- "Who/When" access trail (who accessed model requests / customer data, timestamps, request_id)
- Exportable format for evidence (CSV or JSONL) for ingestion into your internal forensic tools
- 12 months retention as a baseline; possibility to extend to 24 months (TBD)
- Data residency: logs must be stored and exported from US region for this customer
- Transport: SFTP or secure Drive link for delivered exports; signatures to go through procurement

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send a sample export schema (CSV + JSONL example) and a small sample file demonstrating field names and ordering.
2) Monica (CS) will confirm how the export is produced from both Hosted API and Dedicated modes and notes on anonymization/pseudonymization options.
3) Anna to confirm retention target (12 vs 24 months) and preferred delivery method (SFTP / Drive / API pull).
4) Procurement will request standard DPA/SLA language; Ben to loop in Sales Ops if needed.

I’ve attached a tiny sample CSV and the schema doc for quick review. If that looks good, propose a short follow-up on Monday to lock timeline for delivery (estimate 3 business days for initial sample + 5 business days for full evidence pack once fields confirmed).

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_who_when_sample.csv (stub), redwood_export_schema_v1.md (draft)

From: Anna Jones <anna.jones@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Lee <tim.lee@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-09-03T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap — audit log requirements & immediate next steps

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions before we share with procurement: 

1) Delivery format: CSV is preferred. Can you confirm whether CSV will be ordered chronologically (oldest -> newest) and contain separate rows per request? We typically ingest chronological CSV into our SIEM.
2) Fields we must have: timestamp (UTC), internal_user_id (or pseudonym), action (query/create/update), resource_id (customer id/model id), request_id, region. Please confirm exact field names so our parser team can do a quick mapping.
3) Retention: 12 months is our default, but for regulated datasets we may request 24. For now please plan for 12 months and indicate if longer is supported.
4) Residency: must be exported from US data center only. Can you confirm the export endpoint will not route through EU/APAC?

Can you include a one-page table that maps Redwood field -> ACME required field name (so procurement can see exact match)? Once we have that we’ll send a procurement request and loop in legal for DPA language.

—Anna
Anna Jones
Lead Security Engineer | Acme Corp
anna.jones@acme.com

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-09-04T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap — audit log requirements & immediate next steps

Anna — thanks, good questions. Uploading two quick items (attached):
- redwood_export_schema_v1.md — field-by-field mapping + two example export options (CSV chronological & JSONL event-per-line).
- redwood_who_when_sample.csv — 10-line example (fake data) showing header names in CSV order.

Highlights / answers inline: 
- CSV ordering: yes, chronological oldest -> newest by timestamp. Each row = single request/event.
- Required fields included in the schema: timestamp_utc, actor_id (we can provide hashed id or raw internal_user_id per your preference), action, resource_type, resource_id, model_id, request_id, response_size_bytes, region, auth_method. I included a one-row mapping table in the schema matching Redwood->ACME column names.
- Retention: 12 months is standard; we can support 24 months but that requires a config flag and additional storage costs — note this in the schema doc.
- Residency: export process will be initiated from US-hosted exports for ACME accounts; we will not route through EU/APAC for this delivery. Monica has included details below about how we guarantee regional export.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm field mapping & delivery method.
- Mon (09/07): provide a full 3-day sample export (3 months of synthetic events) to SFTP or Drive (your choice).
- If mapping accepted: produce evidence pack (full export + manifest) in 5 business days.

If procurement prefers, we can also provide the same CSV via an S3 presigned URL with limited TTL rather than Drive.

Ben

Attachments: redwood_who_when_sample.csv, redwood_export_schema_v1.md

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Anna Jones <anna.jones@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap — audit log requirements & immediate next steps

Hi Anna — Monica from Customer Success here with the technical details on exports and residency. Forwarding quick notes and a sample schema excerpt.

Export generation notes:
- Hosted API: logs are continuously ingested into our US logging region for ACME accounts. Exports are generated from the US region on request to guarantee residency; we do not proxy through other regions for the export job.
- Dedicated / Private: we can run the export from your VPC or from our Dedicated tenant — both support an identical CSV schema. If you run on-prem, we’ll provide the same export packaging.
- Delivery options: SFTP to customer endpoint, S3 presigned URL, or shared Drive link with restricted access. All transfers are over TLS; we include an MD5 manifest and signed delivery manifest.

Schema excerpt (from redwood_export_schema_v1.md):
- timestamp_utc (ISO-8601)
- actor_id (string) — can be hashed (sha256) on request; mapping table included in schema doc
- action (string) — e.g., GENERATE, EMBED, RERANK
- model_id (string)
- request_id (uuid)
- resource_id (string)
- response_bytes (int)
- region (string)
- auth_method (string)

Sample CSV row (headers omitted here for brevity):
2026-08-01T14:22:03Z, user_17ab3f, GENERATE, gpt-redwood-7b, 8a1d2f3e-..., customer-1234, 2048, us-west-2, api_key

Notes on PII and pseudonymization:
- If ACME requires actor_id to be pseudonymized, we can ship a hashed actor_id column. For forensics, we can also provide a separate identity mapping file under stricter access controls (requires legal/contract approval).
- We do not include full request payloads in the standard audit export; payload capture can be toggled but has storage/retention implications.

I’ve attached the schema doc used by our exports. Happy to run a short demo of the export job for your infra team.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Thanks Ben/Monica — that addresses our questions. Procurement is copied to start the DPA/SLA thread. A few confirmations from ACME side:

- We will proceed with 12 months retention for now. If we request 24 months we will follow up; please include a cost delta in your quote.
- Delivery method: SFTP to our secure ingestion host is preferred. Procurement will send host details in a separate ticket.
- Actor ID: please send hashed actor_id in the initial export, and note how to request an identity mapping if legal approval is obtained.

Next steps from ACME: procurement will open a PO and share DocuSign routing for the DPA. Tim will be the infra lead on the intake — he and Monica should connect for a short runbook/delivery test next week.

Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute call on Wednesday 09/09 at 10am PT to validate the test export?

—Anna
